transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been under a lot of stress lately. Since the foreclosure notices started coming, I haven’t really been myself. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I feel like I’m kind of coming apart—crying in my truck before work, getting jumpy every time the phone rings.

And at work, I’ve been snapping at the apprentices and making dumb mistakes in the repair bay that I never would’ve made before. I’m a mechanic, so that’s not exactly okay. I just… I figured I should talk to someone before I mess things up worse, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family and friends?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped caring completely, but I’ve definitely dropped off from things I used to keep up with. I haven’t been showing up for church volunteering, or my fitness classes, and I’ve skipped the truck-club outings too.

And at work, they’ve actually moved me out of the high-risk repair bay for now, which is… embarrassing to say. I’m trying not to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been affecting more than I wanted to admit.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things even when there isn’t a specific problem at hand, like everyday stuff piling up or things going wrong?

I don’t know if I’d call it worry all the time, exactly. I mean… I’ve got real stuff going on, so it feels kind of tied to that. I haven’t really noticed myself getting worked up over nothing, if that’s what you mean.

Maybe I’m a little more on edge than usual, but I don’t want to overstate it. Does that make sense?
Have you found yourself feeling anxious or tense most days, even when there isn’t anything specific that’s worrying you at the moment?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s most days when there’s nothing specific going on. I mean, if I feel tense, I can usually point to something… or at least I think I can.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just anxious for no reason. Maybe I’m a little keyed up more than I used to be, but I haven’t really noticed it happening out of the blue. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or sad most days, even when there wasn’t a specific reason for it?

I don’t think I’d say “most days,” no. I’ve had some low moments, sure, but usually I can connect it to something that’s going on. It doesn’t feel like I’m just sad out of nowhere all the time.

I mean… maybe I’m not the best judge of it, but I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed yourself feeling anxious or tense even when things are going fine, like in moments when there’s no obvious reason to be upset or worried?

I don’t think so… not in a clear way, anyway. If things are actually fine, I’m usually okay, or at least I haven’t noticed myself getting anxious for no reason.

Sometimes I might still feel a little tense, but I usually assume there’s something behind it, even if I’m not naming it right away. I don’t want to say no if I’m missing something, but I haven’t really caught myself being upset when nothing’s going on.
Have you had times when you felt anxious or noticed physical symptoms like a racing heart or shaking, even when there wasn’t anything specific happening around you to cause that?

I haven’t really noticed that, no… like a racing heart or shaking when nothing’s happening around me. If I do feel worked up, I usually can tie it to something, even if it takes me a minute to figure out what.

I don’t want to say it never happens, because maybe I don’t pay close enough attention to it, but nothing like that stands out to me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed that you’ve been feeling run down or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I’m not really sure… I mean, I get tired like anyone does, but I haven’t noticed it being most days or happening when I haven’t done much.

Maybe I should pay more attention to that, but nothing really stands out to me as feeling unusually run down. Is that an okay way to answer?
Have you noticed yourself worrying about a lot of different things, even when they aren’t necessarily connected to the main problems you’re facing right now?

I don’t think so… not a lot of different things. Mostly if I’m worried, it feels connected to what’s already going on, not random stuff all over the place.

I mean, I can overthink a bit, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. I haven’t really noticed myself jumping from one worry to another about unrelated things. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you found that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even when you’re not thinking about your current problems?

I’m not sure I’d say I no longer take pleasure in things… I mean, I still can enjoy things if I’m actually able to settle into them.

Sometimes it’s harder to get into the mood, especially if stuff is on my mind, but when I’m not thinking about it, I don’t think I’ve completely lost interest or anything like that. Does that answer it the right way?
Have you found yourself feeling worried about different things — even small ones — on more days than not, even when nothing specific is happening to cause it?

I don’t think so… not on more days than not. I mean, little things can bother me here and there, but I wouldn’t say I’m just worried all the time when there’s nothing really causing it.

Mostly if I’m anxious or worked up, there’s usually something specific behind it. I hope that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in most activities, even those you used to enjoy, even when you’re not thinking about your current problems?

I don’t think I’d say most activities, no. I mean… it’s not like everything feels pointless or flat. Some things are harder to enjoy if my mind drifts back to what’s been going on, but if I’m actually distracted or with the right people, I can still get some enjoyment out of things.

So… I don’t think I’ve lost pleasure across the board. Is that the distinction you mean?
Have you had days where you felt down or blue even when nothing particularly bad was happening, and it didn’t seem to be tied to the stress with the foreclosure or work?

I don’t think so… I mean, I have down days, but they usually feel connected to something, like if I’m reminded of the foreclosure stuff or things at work.

If nothing in particular is happening, I can usually be okay. I don’t think it just comes out of nowhere, at least not that I’ve noticed. Is that what you’re asking?
